title: ErrorEraser: Unlearning Data Bias for Improved Continual Learning

problem.claim: Data biases can cause continual-learning models to learn spurious correlations that transfer and amplify across tasks, reducing both knowledge retention and transfer.

gap.claim: Existing continual-learning methods focus on preventing forgetting while ignoring the need to intentionally forget bias-caused erroneous knowledge.

contributions.claim: ErrorEraser is a universal plugin for removing bias-caused erroneous memories in continual learning.
The method combines error identification through feature-space task-data density estimation with error erasure through decision-space shifting for representative outlier samples.
An incremental feature-distribution learning strategy reduces the resource overhead of error identification in downstream tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose the perspective that continual learning requires intentional forgetting in addition to preventing forgetting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Feature-extraction and prediction results indicate that data biases reduce continual learning's ability to retain and transfer knowledge.
Extensive experiments report higher accuracy and lower forgetting rates with ErrorEraser across three types of continual-learning methods.
The authors report that implementation code is available publicly.

narrative_sequence.summary: Continual learning seeks to retain prior knowledge and transfer knowledge to new tasks.
Biases can produce spurious correlations that propagate across tasks, motivating intentional forgetting.
ErrorEraser identifies potentially biased samples and erases only the associated erroneous knowledge.
Incremental feature-distribution learning is used to reduce downstream resource overhead.
Experiments report improved accuracy and reduced forgetting across three continual-learning method types.

unknowns: Datasets, task configurations, baselines, and exact experimental metrics are unspecified.
The abstract does not quantify the reported accuracy gains, forgetting reductions, or resource overhead.
The abstract does not provide implementation details sufficient to reproduce the method.
